transcript.speaker: Ilya Berdysh
transcript.text: Hi Jane, hi Wade, thanks for making time today. Shall we start with a quick round of introductions?

transcript.speaker: Jane Cooper
transcript.text: Sure. I run sales operations at Northwind, we sell warehouse robots to logistics companies.

transcript.speaker: Jane Cooper
transcript.text: Wade leads our account executives, so he is the one living with the problem every day.

transcript.speaker: Wade Warren
transcript.text: Right. My team has about forty customer calls a week and nobody writes proper notes. Deals stall because we forget what was promised.

transcript.speaker: Ilya Berdysh
transcript.text: How do you handle follow-ups today? Is anything recorded in the CRM after a call?

transcript.speaker: Wade Warren
transcript.text: Mostly a two-line summary typed from memory, sometimes nothing. Managers cannot review calls, and onboarding new reps takes months.

transcript.speaker: Jane Cooper
transcript.text: We tried another recorder last year but people disliked the bot joining calls, and the summaries were too generic to be useful.

transcript.speaker: Ilya Berdysh
transcript.text: That is common. With mymeet the transcript and summary land on the company and the people in your CRM automatically, and you can define insight templates per call type.

transcript.speaker: Wade Warren
transcript.text: Templates would help. For discovery calls we follow MEDDPICC, so pain, champion and decision process are what I need.

transcript.speaker: Jane Cooper
transcript.text: On budget: we have money approved for sales tooling this quarter, around twenty thousand dollars per year. The decision is mine together with our CFO.

transcript.speaker: Ilya Berdysh
transcript.text: Great. What would a successful pilot look like for you, and how long should it run?

transcript.speaker: Wade Warren
transcript.text: Two weeks with five reps. If managers can review calls without listening to them and notes are complete, that is a win.

transcript.speaker: Jane Cooper
transcript.text: And security review: our IT team needs the data processing agreement before anyone installs anything.

transcript.speaker: Ilya Berdysh
transcript.text: Understood. I will send the DPA and a pilot proposal by Friday, and set up the five seats once IT approves.

transcript.speaker: Jane Cooper
transcript.text: Perfect. Let us reconvene next Thursday to kick off the pilot.
